# Common Practice

Use plain, simple Australian English. Explain code in concrete words.

Read [README.md](README.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), and
[the documentation index](docs/README.md) before changing the repository.

## Mandatory implementation rules

Apply [development-workflows:strict-effect-ts](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md)
to **all owned code**, including tests, scripts, configuration and infrastructure.
Use Effect for every operation that can fail or perform work outside the program.
Use Effect Schema to check inputs and outputs and branded types for identifiers,
paths and meaningful strings at boundaries. Keep errors typed and named.

Declare owned Effect Layers as static values. Supply dependencies through their
Requirements type channel, using native `Layer.succeed` at composition sites and
`Layer.mock` or replacement Layers in tests. Native composition callbacks are
allowed; do not wrap a Layer in an owned factory function.

No raw async/await or Promise workflows, try/catch, throws, fetch, process.env,
unchecked JSON, unchecked array indexing, assertions, unsafe Option extraction,
ambient clocks, or mutable global collections. Prefer Effect primitives first.
Plain JSX and deterministic framework declarations are allowed.
The only command runtimes are `tools/references/sync.runtime.ts` and
`tools/checks/docs.runtime.ts`; test execution belongs to @effect/vitest.
The frontend runtime is `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`: one runtime whose
single runner every TanStack entry point uses. Keep TanStack response adaptation
there. The Website calls its same-stage API through
`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts`, the checked adapter using Alchemy's public `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient`.
`apps/web/src/lib/api/cloudflare.ingress.ts` reads the host bindings through a normal
Cloudflare import and composes the live WebsiteApi Layer. Keep host-independent
validation and forwarding testable without importing that host module.
The native API entry `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` composes
Content, the private renderer and shared transport Layers. Its HTTP handler runs
in the incoming request's Effect fibre without another Promise runner. Do not
pass Effect Context through TanStack or add another frontend runtime.
Image SDK calls stay in `apps/api/src/og/takumi.adapter.layer.ts`.
PostHog browser SDK calls stay in `apps/web/src/lib/analytics/browser.adapter.layer.ts`;
Distilled management calls stay in `packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/management.adapter.layer.ts`.
Backend analytics uses Effect HttpClient and native Alchemy `waitUntil`.

Authored marketing Markdown belongs to `@content/pages`; training MDX and the
single ordered outline per course belong to `@content/training`.
`@common-practice/training` owns course/chapter schemas, checked course services,
immutable progress rules and native Atom definitions. It reuses Content's PageId;
Content never imports Training. Training adds no runtime or separate writable
progress service. `@common-practice/content` owns page schemas,
errors, service, source loader and live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and MCP reuse those
exports. No package imports an app. Keep one `getPage({ id, format })` operation,
with optional `format` defaulting to complete `data`; check the returned variant.
Frontend loaders preserve typed errors in a checked success/error envelope.

The browser runtime is `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts`, an Effect Atom
runtime mounted by React. Its Promise bridges are confined to
`apps/web/src/lib/webmcp/model-context.adapter.layer.ts` and the private browser
analytics adapter. PostHog's synchronous before-send callback is confined to
`apps/web/src/lib/analytics/capture.consumer.ts`; it uses a non-throwing Schema
check and returns only allowed fields. Browser content calls
use the public API and checked addresses from the root loader, not bundled
sources. WebMCP registers only at the matching Website origin. Remote MCP has a
separate public checked Origin/CORS policy. Keep server and browser runtime
imports inside TanStack's matching environment functions (`lib/browser-atom.ts`
is the browser one). Follow the ownership sections in ARCHITECTURE.md.

Apply [development-workflows:alchemy-iac](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/SKILL.md)
to deployment work. Only the native Alchemy CLI may plan, deploy or destroy.
Never substitute Wrangler or provider API writes for Alchemy resource ownership.
Check `.references/alchemy` examples and installed types before implementation.
Check `.references/effect` for current Effect APIs. Run `bun run references:sync`
to verify both reference clones against the committed lock and package catalog.
Do not modify the reference clones or copy legacy Site patches blindly.

Every dependency must have an exact current, compatible release recorded in the
root catalogs or manifest. Refresh registry metadata before changing versions.
Follow [version decisions](docs/standards/dependencies.md); stable Effect v4
matches native Alchemy v2's supported peer version.

## Checks and boundaries

Run `bun run verification` before claiming the local implementation passes.
The build generates TanStack's route tree; never edit that generated file.
Keep `tools/oxlint/vendor` byte-for-byte reference copies, with provenance and
rule dispositions in [lint policy](docs/standards/lint.md). New rules and tests
must follow Effect. Never disable a failing safety rule just to get green checks.
Prove important prohibitions using the actual Oxlint command and negative fixtures.

Keep local checks, browser checks, Cloudflare deployment and public URL checks
as separate evidence. A local build does not prove a working deployment.
Credentials belong in Doppler or the ignored `.env`; `.env` overrides Doppler
in every stack, and shell settings are disabled. Native provider sign-in uses
the runner's scoped `DOPPLER_TOKEN` or Alchemy profile. Never print credentials,
commit them, or forward the
whole environment into a Worker. The Website declares its bindings explicitly:
`COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`, its stage-specific `BACKEND` service binding, `COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`,
`COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL`, `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG`. Cloudflare delivers logs
and traces to Axiom; neither Worker binds direct exporter credentials or emits custom metrics. Both Workers use native Alchemy
ownership and deploy together; Preview APIs must never point to production.
Do not adopt existing cloud resources or configure a public domain by guesswork.

Before changing an area, read its owning document. Update that document when
behaviour changes; do not create competing instructions. Preserve unrelated work.

## Shared development skills

Before starting work, follow [the plugin lookup](docs/skills.md) and load the
latest published Commonplace `development-workflows` plugin. Do not use saved
repository copies or assume a cached plugin version is current. Read the local
profiles in `docs/skill-profiles/` alongside the plugin.
# Common Practice

Common Practice is live at <https://withcommonpractice.com>, with its API at
<https://api.withcommonpractice.com>. The repository, packages, Workers, bindings,
Doppler project and active artwork now use the new name. Old website links redirect
with their path and query; the old API stays available for existing clients.
See the [cutover checklist](docs/exec-plans/common-practice-cutover-checklist.md)
for completed work, retained historical identifiers and the remaining external items.

A website for corporate teams, with Home, About and Contact pages. Built with
TanStack Start, React, Effect and native Alchemy on Cloudflare. The website
includes a checked HTTP API, RPC, read-only MCP, SEO/AEO discovery files,
agent discovery (named AI crawler rules with Content Signals, an Agent Skills
index, an MCP server card and in-browser WebMCP tools) and generated social
images, all using the same authored page content. The Contact form is a UI preview;
sending is not available. Local changes need a separate release before they appear online.

## Run locally

Use Bun 1.4.2 and Node 24. The lockfile pins every package resolution.

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run references:sync
bun run dev
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:3210>. `dev` runs native Alchemy with the explicit
`dev` stage and Doppler config `common-practice/dev`. Set up native Alchemy's
Doppler profile first, as shown in the [deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md#native-local-development).
Every stack reads Doppler, then the optional ignored `.env`; `.env` wins.
Shell settings do not override either source.

The matching API runs at <http://127.0.0.1:3211>. Both apps run through native
Alchemy; there is no single-app backend fallback.
The workspace includes Bun 1.4.2 as a development dependency; use
`./node_modules/.bin/bun` if the global Bun version is older.

```sh
bun run verification
```

This builds the generated route tree, checks formatting, runs strict Oxlint and
Effect diagnostics, checks TypeScript, runs tests, checks unused files and
validates the documentation index.

## Repository map

- `apps/web`: the standard TanStack frontend and browser WebMCP host.
- `apps/api`: the native Effect API Worker, publishing routes and image renderer.
- `content/pages`: authored Markdown in `@content/pages`.
- `packages`: shared Appearance, Training, Content, HTTP, RPC, MCP, analytics and infrastructure owners.
- `alchemy.run.ts`: native Alchemy entry point for the `common-practice` Website and Backend stack.
- `alchemy.axiom.run.ts` and `alchemy.trace.run.ts`: the production-only
  `common-practice-observability` and `common-practice-trace-export` stacks.
- `alchemy.posthog.run.ts`: the `common-practice-analytics` stack for Common Practice production/Preview
  projects, dashboards and their charts.
- `test`: the opt-in Alchemy integration suite.
- `.github/workflows`: verification checks, pull-request Preview and manual production
  deployments.
- `docs`: the [documentation index](docs/README.md): design, runbooks, standards and dated evidence.
- `tools`: Effect command programs and lint enforcement tests.
- `.references`: ignored, locked upstream Effect and Alchemy source clones.
- `.agents/skills`: portable implementation guidance; `.claude/skills` links here.

Read [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [documentation](docs/README.md),
[lint policy](docs/standards/lint.md), [dependency choices](docs/standards/dependencies.md)
and the [deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md).

The pages introduce strategy, training, forward-deployed engineering,
deployments and agent builds. The cream layouts use a brown/gold halftone band
and navy cross pattern. The header and favicon use Paper's original Common
Practice tile and outlined wordmark. The decorative patterns repeat that same
tile. [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) records the confirmed audience and scope;
[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) records the implemented visual system.
[Appearance](packages/appearance/README.md) is a separate Effect-only package
with checked theme-switching actions. Other repositories can copy it and supply
their own runtime, identifiers and colours.
Preview Website responses and static assets carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.

Open sample training starts at `/training`: Claude for Beginners, Codex for
Beginners and Agentic AI for Legal Work. Each course has three chapters and six
pages, with explicit completion and browser-saved resume. Authored MDX lives in
`@content/training`; checked course logic and native progress atoms belong to
`@common-practice/training`. The [implementation ledger](docs/exec-plans/training-course-design.md)
records checks and release proof separately.

## AI work history

[Entire](https://entire.io) records both Codex and Claude Code chats and tool
activity alongside Git commits. This repository was configured with Entire CLI
0.11.3. Install Entire on each machine, then run from this checkout:

```sh
entire enable --agent codex --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire enable --agent claude-code --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire status
```

Open `/hooks` in Codex and approve the seven Entire commands. Both Codex and
Claude Code must start a fresh chat after setup so Entire can record each chat
from the beginning. `entire doctor` checks the installed commands and their
approval records.

The shared configuration is in `.entire/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json` and
`.claude/settings.json`. Run the setup commands above in every clone, so Git's
automatic recording commands are installed there too. Entire's local logs,
working chat copies and machine-specific settings are ignored by Git. Anonymous
usage reporting is off.

Commits create checkpoints, stored as separate Git references. The shared
settings select `origin` for chat uploads, so new working copies use the same
destination. Pushing to `origin` syncs those checkpoints, including chat text
and tool activity. Entire uploads to one selected remote; a push directly to
`upstream` does not upload the chat records. New chat activity after a push
waits for the next push.
Commit linking is automatic (`commit_linking: "always"`). For chats that change
files, finish the normal workflow with `git commit` and `git push origin`; the
installed Git commands create and upload the record. Ending a chat alone does
not publish it online. Chats without a file change can be published using the
explicit backfill workflow below.
This follows [Entire's documented workflow](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart).
Entire removes detected secrets before saving checkpoints, but this check can
miss things. Keep credentials out of chats and review what you share. Existing
chat history is not imported by the setup command above.

The repository's Entire page is <https://entire.io/gh/crcorbett/common-practice>. Its hosted
connection keeps a private copy of the repository in Australia (Sydney). This
connection is separate from the local recording setup. This checkout's `origin`
uses the Sydney mirror; the direct GitHub URL is preserved as `upstream`. The
mirror sends ordinary code pushes through to GitHub and stores chat records.
To configure another clone for the same mirror, run:

```sh
git remote rename origin upstream
entire repo remote add origin /gh/crcorbett/common-practice --cluster aws-ap-southeast-2.entire.io
entire enable --agent codex --checkpoint-push-remote origin --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire status
```

The destination command also repairs an older local choice. Check that
`entire status` names `origin`. Each existing working copy can have its own
`.entire/settings.local.json` override; keep its destination on `origin` too.

### Backfill existing chats

Entire CLI 0.10.5 can import existing Codex and Claude Code transcripts as
read-only checkpoints. Run a preview before importing:

```sh
entire import codex --dry-run
entire import claude-code --dry-run
entire import codex
entire import claude-code
```

The importer normally reads files changed in the past 30 days. It skips turns
already imported. Use `--session <id>` to select particular chats and `--path`
to select a transcript folder. Codex matches each chat's recorded working
folder; its default scan misses compressed archives and Common Practice's former Google
Drive location. The September 2026 backfill uses temporary, decompressed copies
of the selected chats, with only their initial working-folder field changed to
this checkout. Originals stay untouched. Claude Code's former project folder
can be selected directly with `--path`.

Imported chats can be searched and read, but cannot be resumed through Entire.
Sync them with the installed command `entire hooks git pre-push origin`, then
check the hosted Sessions page. This sync uploads checkpoint data without
pushing source changes. Use the Sydney mirror for `origin`: the initial backfill
reached GitHub, but its checkpoint references did not reach the hosted Sessions
page until they were pushed directly to the mirror. Ordinary Claude web, desktop
and Cowork chats have no direct importer in this CLI version.

## Live preview

Every hosted Preview stage has its own Alchemy-managed Website and API Workers.
After deploying stage `preview`, its Website address is
<https://common-practice-preview.coopercorbett.workers.dev>. See the deployment
runbook for Doppler configuration and the reviewed plan/deploy process.

Each same-repository pull request gets its own stage
`pr-<number>`, deployed by the **Pull request preview** workflow. The workflow
comments the Preview URL on the pull request and destroys the Preview when the
pull request closes. Fork pull requests are skipped.

`bun run test:integration` deploys the `integration` Preview, checks Home,
About, a missing page and the matching API’s `/pages`, then destroys it. It changes
Cloudflare, needs Doppler's `common-practice/stg_preview` credentials and is not part of
`verification`; run it only with authorisation.

## Production

Private source repository: <https://github.com/crcorbett/common-practice>.
Live website: <https://withcommonpractice.com>.
API: <https://api.withcommonpractice.com>; RPC `/rpc`, remote MCP `/mcp`.
Production uses stage `production` and Doppler config `common-practice/prd`:

```sh
bun run production:plan
bun run production:deploy --yes
```

GitHub Actions has a manual **Deploy production** workflow on `main`. It checks
the selected commit and uses the same native Alchemy scripts and cloud state.
See the deployment runbook for credential rotation and deployment coordination.

## Observability

Product analytics uses PostHog separately from request telemetry. The browser's
existing Effect Atom runtime records explicit page views and selected navigation
automatically on enabled deployments, while honouring Do Not Track. Browser
batches pass through `/ingest/e/` on the Website to reduce domain blocking;
occasional loss remains possible. The API counts its own requests and completed content reads,
with short sends in native Alchemy background work. Ordinary Previews and local
development keep collection off. A separate Alchemy stack owns production/Preview
PostHog projects and two private dashboards in each. See the

```

A service token can read only its own config. Use a separate profile for each

```

### Runtime settings

Alchemy supplies the existing named bindings to both applications. Keep the API
address tied to that stage's Backend output and each app's self address tied to
native `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`. Shared Config declarations and the checks they
reuse are described in [host settings](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#host-settings).

| Binding                          | Required behaviour                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`          | Use the declared stage. An invalid API stage stops startup. A missing or invalid Website stage returns its unavailable configuration result. The same declaration is reused by telemetry. |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`        | Supply the canonical API origin, without a trailing slash, credentials, path, query or fragment. Both apps and MCP reuse the checked declaration.                                         |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL`    | Supply the native Website self URL. Its root slash is accepted, but credentials, paths, queries and fragments are rejected.                                                               |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG` | Missing, invalid or differently staged settings keep capture off. Production and test project checks are retained.                                                                        |

The API reads required settings during native startup. The Website reads public
settings once when its existing server runtime starts on the first request;
address or stage failures return its unavailable configuration result. Settings change
with a new runtime, so deploy the changed bindings together with the matching
code. Browser configuration contains only the checked public addresses and
capture settings; management credentials and telemetry tokens remain private.

### Training release checks

The accepted training plan authorises public sample-course release and indexing.
Training changes update the existing Website and its matching Backend through
the joint native Alchemy stack. They add no provider resources, domains,
credentials, PostHog projects or dashboards. Review the exact stage's plan and
keep Preview bindings pointed to its own API. A test-enabled Preview uses the
existing Common Practice preview analytics project; restore normal disabled
Preview capture after stored-event checks.

Before release, run full verification and complete the three browser journeys,
including phone/desktop, keyboard, reload/resume, explicit complete/undo and
confirmed course-isolated reset. After apply, read back both native owners and
run the public suite against both output addresses. It checks 21 page bodies and
representations, three course outlines through HTTP/RPC/MCP, discovery, nested
Website text/image links and uncached missing/invalid training responses.
Separately verify deliberate learning actions as actually stored PostHog events.
Record results and limits in the training ledger/evidence; local success is
not hosted proof. Roll back using the recorded pre-release revision through
native Alchemy's joint deployment, retaining existing projects and event history.

### Commands

Run `bun run verification` first. Select the native Doppler profile locally,
or supply the config-scoped `DOPPLER_TOKEN` in CI. The stage-specific native plan
loads and checks the resolved configuration, including the account ID's form.
The old `production:check-env` and `pr:check-env` commands are removed: the
native provider preflight reads exported variables before stack secrets load
and cannot check this stage-specific configuration. Review the plan;
reject unexpected deletion, adoption, state-store upgrades or changes to another
application. After authorising that plan, use the corresponding deploy command:

```sh
bun run preview:plan
bun run preview:deploy --yes

bun run production:plan
bun run production:deploy --yes
```

The default deploy scripts omit `--yes`. It is needed for an authorised apply
in a non-interactive terminal. Native Alchemy recalculates the plan on apply.
Production serves from `withcommonpractice.com` (see Custom domain below).
Production scaffold content is indexable, so its placeholder wording may appear
in search results. Non-production Website responses and workers.dev static
assets carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.

`Cloudflare.state()` uses the account's native state store, partitioned by stack
and stage. Its first use can bootstrap resources, and a cold login can use a
temporary edge-preview session to read the state authentication secret.
Cloudflare requires Secrets Store Edit to attach that temporary secret binding;
Read only covers metadata and cannot complete a fresh login. Edit also permits
creating, changing and deleting secrets across the account. Cooper explicitly
approved this additional permission after a fresh GitHub run exposed the
Read-only limitation. See [Cloudflare access control](https://developers.cloudflare.com/secrets-store/access-control/).
A state-store upgrade or any other permission expansion remains a separate
maintenance task. Preserve the existing shared store and other applications;
do not switch to local state to bypass an authentication failure.

provider readback, browser and public checks in dated evidence. A final native
plan should report no changes; production drift must be read for reported drift,
because its successful exit is not a no-drift assertion. Never use `--repair`
as a substitute for an authorised plan/apply. Recovery deploys a known-good
revision through native Alchemy; do not bypass the owner with provider writes.

## Telemetry checks

Run these after a change to the telemetry Layer, the request observer, the
bindings or the dashboards. The design and reasons are in the
[observability plan](../exec-plans/observability.md). Record what you observe as a
dated file under `docs/evidence/observability/`, with the revision, stage, window
and figures. Do not copy provider state into a living document, and never put a
token in a command line, log or record.

**Authority.** The Preview deploy needs the reviewed plan and authorisation
(see Plan and deploy). The Axiom queries below only read. Use the read access of
the Common Practice management credential (`AXIOM_TOKEN` in `common-practice/prd`) or the Axiom web app.

### Log and trace delivery on a Preview

Request unique uncached Website URLs and one API machine route. Record the bounded
time window and deployment ids. Query Axiom for new JSON console request records
from both Workers; check stage, worker, response outcome and isolate identity.
Inspect the actual body envelope before using the shared dashboard reader. Verify
that logs contain no request bodies, credentials or raw user agents. Cloudflare
invocation records are separate and must not be counted as application records.

Wait for both signals to arrive before comparing counts. Confirm connected native
traces and no Worker-side calls to Axiom log or metric endpoints. There is no new
metric point to reconcile. Historical metric data is retained without live metric
panels. Log/trace delivery is best effort; successful requests alone do not prove
stored records, and records present do not establish lossless delivery.

### Isolate attributes on a Preview

Website request logs carry `requestSeq`, `isolateId` and `routeFamily`. The first
request in an isolate has sequence 1. Query those logs with the automatic root
span using their shared `trace_id`; wait for both signals before comparing counts.
The latency dashboard uses Cloudflare CPU time and log-derived cold/warm labels.
Missing logs remain unlabelled. The API retains native Alchemy Effect spans;
the Website has no custom span and no startup-time estimate. Do not treat root
span duration as visitor response time or infer cold starts from slow responses.

### Dashboards

The five Common Practice dashboards change only through `bun run axiom:plan` and
`bun run axiom:deploy --yes`. A plan for a dashboard-only change must show updates
to `CommonPracticeRequestOverview`, `CommonPracticeRequestFailures`,
`CommonPracticeRequestLatency`, `CommonPracticeTraffic` and `CommonPracticeTelemetryHealth`
and no other resource. Check the render, not only the plan:

1. Open each dashboard with `?v_stage=production`.
2. Keep the browser tab visible. A hidden tab never fills its panels, and a
   screenshot makes the tab visible.
3. Scroll every panel into view, because Axiom loads panels lazily.
4. Wait for the spinners to clear, then take the screenshot. One taken as a panel
   fills shows it blank.
5. Check a phone width (390 px) for the note, the tiles and the tables.

The [dashboard design](../exec-plans/observability-dashboards.md) says what each
panel answers and the rules its queries follow. To roll back, revert the change
and run `bun run axiom:deploy --yes` again. The dashboards are updated in place,
so a revert is an update, not a delete.

**Escalation.** A count that will not match, or a panel that stays empty, goes
into the plan's Open items with the query and window. Do not disable a check or
edit a dashboard in Axiom's web app to make it pass.

## Public page caching

Native `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` sets `cache.enabled: true`. The separate
`enable_request_signal` compatibility flag supports request cancellation; a
Preview test confirmed that page caching and MCP and RPC POSTs work with that
flag off. The cause of earlier POST hangs remains unproved. Cache entries stay
with one Worker version; a new deployment starts cold. Safe public HTML,
Markdown, social images and discovery text advertise the Site-style browser
and CDN lifetimes described in [architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).
Only the public page API list and its two checked detail paths join that
policy; the API catalogue, OpenAPI document, RPC, MCP, error and cookie
responses remain `no-store`. Static assets are cached separately by Cloudflare.
Require repeated public GETs to show a `CF-Cache-Status` hit at one Cloudflare
location, and test real MCP and RPC POSTs in both Preview and production. A
future personalised page requires a cache-policy change first.

### When GitHub Actions cannot start

Read the failed job's annotations first. If account usage, spending, payment or
runner limits prevented the job from starting, run the same checks and native
deployment commands locally. A failed build or test still needs fixing; local
execution does not turn a failed GitHub check into a passing one.

lockfile. Confirm the production workflow is idle before a local apply. Use
the existing Doppler configuration and native Alchemy state; do not change
credentials, state ownership or branch protections to work around CI limits.

```sh

bun run references:sync
bun run verification
bun run production:plan

bun run production:drift --no-input
COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_WEBSITE_URL=https://withcommonpractice.com \
COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_API_URL=https://api.withcommonpractice.com bun run test:public
bun run production:plan

Record the blocked GitHub run, exact commit, local check results, reviewed plan,

## Removal policies

Production's Website and Backend, Common Practice's Axiom ingest token, its five dashboards and the
`common-practice-axiom-traces` destination use `RemovalPolicy.retain`. Removing their
declaration or destroying their stack drops Alchemy's record but leaves the
cloud object running. Every Preview stays destroyable. A removal policy is not
a prop: a plan shows no change, and the next deploy of each stack records it.
Until then, the old destroy policy is still in state. The Axiom token has no
update API, so changing its props replaces it and leaves the old token live in
Axiom. Revoke that old token deliberately after the new one is proven.

Website and API URLs are checked through native `Output.mapEffect` when Alchemy
resolves them. Its callback has no error channel in the locked beta.81 release,
so an invalid URL stops resolution with `WebsiteOutputError` or `ApiOutputError`
as the fatal cause. A failed output check does not prove the Worker was rolled back.

The former `WebsiteOutput` Action declaration is removed. On the next separately
authorised native plan, Alchemy lists its saved Action record for deletion; the
following authorised apply drops that record without running the old Action
body or deleting a Worker. This follows beta.79's native `Plan.ts` and `Apply.ts`
Action-removal behaviour. Review that state-only removal alongside the Worker
changes. Do not manually edit cloud state or run a separate destroy to remove it.
Local URL tests prove checking, not removal of a hosted saved record.

## Verification record

The [dated record](../evidence/bootstrap/local-verification.md) contains the
initial preview, local production and GitHub deployment evidence, followed by
the dedicated-credential and native-local-development checks. Historical checks
retain their original credential and revision context.
name: Checks
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: checks-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.2"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run verification
name: Pull request preview
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, closed]
permissions:
  contents: read
# Deploy and destroy mutate the same pr-<number> stage, so they never overlap.
# Each run reads the pull request's current state before it mutates anything.
concurrency:
  group: common-practice-pr-${{ github.event.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
env:
  STAGE: pr-${{ github.event.number }}
jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Deploy preview
    # Fork pull requests never receive the preview credential.
    if: >-
      github.event.action != 'closed' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    environment:
      name: preview
      url: https://common-practice-pr-${{ github.event.number }}.coopercorbett.workers.dev
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.2"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run verification
      - name: Check that the pull request is still open
        id: pull-request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          state="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}" --jq .state)"
          echo "open=$([ "$state" = open ] && echo true || echo false)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Supply checked deployment metadata through .env
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.open == 'true'
        env:
          PULL_REQUEST: ${{ github.event.number }}
          BUILD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          printf '%s\n' "GITHUB_ACTIONS=$GITHUB_ACTIONS" "GITHUB_SHA=$GITHUB_SHA" "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER" "GITHUB_REPOSITORY=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "PULL_REQUEST=$PULL_REQUEST" "BUILD_SHA=$BUILD_SHA" > .env
      - name: Plan preview with native Alchemy
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.open == 'true'
        run: bun run pr:deploy "$STAGE" --dry-run
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Deploy preview with native Alchemy
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.open == 'true'
        run: bun run pr:deploy "$STAGE" --yes
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Check Website and public API
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.open == 'true'
        run: bun run test:public
        env:
          COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_WEBSITE_URL: https://common-practice-pr-${{ github.event.number }}.coopercorbett.workers.dev
          COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_API_URL: https://common-practice-pr-${{ github.event.number }}-backend.coopercorbett.workers.dev
  cleanup:
    name: Destroy preview
    if: >-
      github.event.action == 'closed' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    environment:
      name: preview
    steps:
      # Destroy with the code that deployed this stage.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.2"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Check that the pull request is closed
        id: pull-request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          state="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}" --jq .state)"
          echo "closed=$([ "$state" = closed ] && echo true || echo false)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # Allowlist, not denylist: cleanup only ever destroys pr-<number> stages.
      # `pr:destroy` repeats this check before it loads any credential.
      - name: Safety check
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.closed == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ ! "$STAGE" =~ ^pr-[1-9][0-9]{0,6}$ ]]; then
            echo "Cleanup only destroys pr-<number> stages, got '$STAGE'" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Supply checked deployment metadata through .env
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.closed == 'true'
        env:
          PULL_REQUEST: ${{ github.event.number }}
          BUILD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          printf '%s\n' "GITHUB_ACTIONS=$GITHUB_ACTIONS" "GITHUB_SHA=$GITHUB_SHA" "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER" "GITHUB_REPOSITORY=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "PULL_REQUEST=$PULL_REQUEST" "BUILD_SHA=$BUILD_SHA" > .env
      - name: Destroy preview with native Alchemy
        if: steps.pull-request.outputs.closed == 'true'
        run: bun run pr:destroy "$STAGE" --yes
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
name: Deploy production
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: Re-upload the current version even when unchanged
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: common-practice-production
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  deploy:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://withcommonpractice.com
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.2"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run verification
      - name: Supply checked deployment metadata through .env
        env:
          BUILD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          printf '%s\n' "GITHUB_ACTIONS=$GITHUB_ACTIONS" "GITHUB_SHA=$GITHUB_SHA" "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER" "GITHUB_REPOSITORY=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "BUILD_SHA=$BUILD_SHA" > .env
      - name: Plan production with native Alchemy
        run: bun run production:deploy --dry-run ${{ inputs.force && '--force' || '' }}
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      - name: Deploy production with native Alchemy
        run: bun run production:deploy --yes ${{ inputs.force && '--force' || '' }}
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      # Re-observes every deployed resource against the state Alchemy just wrote.
      # It reports drift; it never repairs it.
      - name: Read back provider drift with native Alchemy
        run: bun run production:drift --no-input
        env:
          DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      - name: Check Website and public API
        run: bun run test:public
        env:
          COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_WEBSITE_URL: https://withcommonpractice.com
          COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_API_URL: https://api.withcommonpractice.com

# Common Practice

Use plain, simple Australian English. Explain code in concrete words.

Read [README.md](README.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), and
[the documentation index](docs/README.md) before changing the repository.

## Mandatory implementation rules

Apply [development-workflows:strict-effect-ts](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md)
to **all owned code**, including tests, scripts, configuration and infrastructure.
Use Effect for every operation that can fail or perform work outside the program.
Use Effect Schema to check inputs and outputs and branded types for identifiers,
paths and meaningful strings at boundaries. Keep errors typed and named.

Declare owned Effect Layers as static values. Supply dependencies through their
Requirements type channel, using native `Layer.succeed` at composition sites and
`Layer.mock` or replacement Layers in tests. Native composition callbacks are
allowed; do not wrap a Layer in an owned factory function.

No raw async/await or Promise workflows, try/catch, throws, fetch, process.env,
unchecked JSON, unchecked array indexing, assertions, unsafe Option extraction,
ambient clocks, or mutable global collections. Prefer Effect primitives first.
Plain JSX and deterministic framework declarations are allowed.
The only command runtimes are `tools/references/sync.runtime.ts` and
`tools/checks/docs.runtime.ts`; test execution belongs to @effect/vitest.
The frontend runtime is `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`: one runtime whose
single runner every TanStack entry point uses. Keep TanStack response adaptation
there. The Website calls its same-stage API through
`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts`, the checked adapter using Alchemy's public `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient`.
`apps/web/src/lib/api/cloudflare.ingress.ts` reads the host bindings through a normal
Cloudflare import and composes the live WebsiteApi Layer. Keep host-independent
validation and forwarding testable without importing that host module.
The native API entry `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` composes
Content, the private renderer and shared transport Layers. Its HTTP handler runs
in the incoming request's Effect fibre without another Promise runner. Do not
pass Effect Context through TanStack or add another frontend runtime.
Image SDK calls stay in `apps/api/src/og/takumi.adapter.layer.ts`.
PostHog browser SDK calls stay in `apps/web/src/lib/analytics/browser.adapter.layer.ts`;
Distilled management calls stay in `packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/management.adapter.layer.ts`.
Backend analytics uses Effect HttpClient and native Alchemy `waitUntil`.

Authored marketing Markdown belongs to `@content/pages`; training MDX and the
single ordered outline per course belong to `@content/training`.
`@common-practice/training` owns course/chapter schemas, checked course services,
immutable progress rules and native Atom definitions. It reuses Content's PageId;
Content never imports Training. Training adds no runtime or separate writable
progress service. `@common-practice/content` owns page schemas,
errors, service, source loader and live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and MCP reuse those
exports. No package imports an app. Keep one `getPage({ id, format })` operation,
with optional `format` defaulting to complete `data`; check the returned variant.
Frontend loaders preserve typed errors in a checked success/error envelope.

The browser runtime is `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts`, an Effect Atom
runtime mounted by React. Its Promise bridges are confined to
`apps/web/src/lib/webmcp/model-context.adapter.layer.ts` and the private browser
analytics adapter. PostHog's synchronous before-send callback is confined to
`apps/web/src/lib/analytics/capture.consumer.ts`; it uses a non-throwing Schema
check and returns only allowed fields. Browser content calls
use the public API and checked addresses from the root loader, not bundled
sources. WebMCP registers only at the matching Website origin. Remote MCP has a
separate public checked Origin/CORS policy. Keep server and browser runtime
imports inside TanStack's matching environment functions (`lib/browser-atom.ts`
is the browser one). Follow the ownership sections in ARCHITECTURE.md.

Apply [development-workflows:alchemy-iac](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/alchemy-iac/SKILL.md)
to deployment work. Only the native Alchemy CLI may plan, deploy or destroy.
Never substitute Wrangler or provider API writes for Alchemy resource ownership.
Check `.references/alchemy` examples and installed types before implementation.
Check `.references/effect` for current Effect APIs. Run `bun run references:sync`
to verify both reference clones against the committed lock and package catalog.
Do not modify the reference clones or copy legacy Site patches blindly.

Every dependency must have an exact current, compatible release recorded in the
root catalogs or manifest. Refresh registry metadata before changing versions.
Follow [version decisions](docs/standards/dependencies.md); stable Effect v4
matches native Alchemy v2's supported peer version.

## Checks and boundaries

Run `bun run verification` before claiming the local implementation passes.
The build generates TanStack's route tree; never edit that generated file.
Keep `tools/oxlint/vendor` byte-for-byte reference copies, with provenance and
rule dispositions in [lint policy](docs/standards/lint.md). New rules and tests
must follow Effect. Never disable a failing safety rule just to get green checks.
Prove important prohibitions using the actual Oxlint command and negative fixtures.

Keep local checks, browser checks, Cloudflare deployment and public URL checks
as separate evidence. A local build does not prove a working deployment.
Credentials belong in Doppler or the ignored `.env`; `.env` overrides Doppler
in every stack, and shell settings are disabled. Native provider sign-in uses
the runner's scoped `DOPPLER_TOKEN` or Alchemy profile. Never print credentials,
commit them, or forward the
whole environment into a Worker. The Website declares its bindings explicitly:
`COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`, its stage-specific `BACKEND` service binding, `COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`,
`COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL`, `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG`. Cloudflare delivers logs
and traces to Axiom; neither Worker binds direct exporter credentials or emits custom metrics. Both Workers use native Alchemy
ownership and deploy together; Preview APIs must never point to production.
Do not adopt existing cloud resources or configure a public domain by guesswork.

Before changing an area, read its owning document. Update that document when
behaviour changes; do not create competing instructions. Preserve unrelated work.

## Shared development skills

Before starting work, follow [the plugin lookup](docs/skills.md) and load the
latest published Commonplace `development-workflows` plugin. Do not use saved
repository copies or assume a cached plugin version is current. Read the local
profiles in `docs/skill-profiles/` alongside the plugin.
# Common Practice

Common Practice is live at <https://withcommonpractice.com>, with its API at
<https://api.withcommonpractice.com>. The repository, packages, Workers, bindings,
Doppler project and active artwork now use the new name. Old website links redirect
with their path and query; the old API stays available for existing clients.
See the [cutover checklist](docs/exec-plans/common-practice-cutover-checklist.md)
for completed work, retained historical identifiers and the remaining external items.

A website for corporate teams, with Home, About and Contact pages. Built with
TanStack Start, React, Effect and native Alchemy on Cloudflare. The website
includes a checked HTTP API, RPC, read-only MCP, SEO/AEO discovery files,
agent discovery (named AI crawler rules with Content Signals, an Agent Skills
index, an MCP server card and in-browser WebMCP tools) and generated social
images, all using the same authored page content. The Contact form is a UI preview;
sending is not available. Local changes need a separate release before they appear online.

## Run locally

Use Bun 1.4.2 and Node 24. The lockfile pins every package resolution.

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run references:sync
bun run dev
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:3210>. `dev` runs native Alchemy with the explicit
`dev` stage and Doppler config `common-practice/dev`. Set up native Alchemy's
Doppler profile first, as shown in the [deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md#native-local-development).
Every stack reads Doppler, then the optional ignored `.env`; `.env` wins.
Shell settings do not override either source.

The matching API runs at <http://127.0.0.1:3211>. Both apps run through native
Alchemy; there is no single-app backend fallback.
The workspace includes Bun 1.4.2 as a development dependency; use
`./node_modules/.bin/bun` if the global Bun version is older.

```sh
bun run verification
```

This builds the generated route tree, checks formatting, runs strict Oxlint and
Effect diagnostics, checks TypeScript, runs tests, checks unused files and
validates the documentation index.

## Repository map

- `apps/web`: the standard TanStack frontend and browser WebMCP host.
- `apps/api`: the native Effect API Worker, publishing routes and image renderer.
- `content/pages`: authored Markdown in `@content/pages`.
- `packages`: shared Appearance, Training, Content, HTTP, RPC, MCP, analytics and infrastructure owners.
- `alchemy.run.ts`: native Alchemy entry point for the `common-practice` Website and Backend stack.
- `alchemy.axiom.run.ts` and `alchemy.trace.run.ts`: the production-only
  `common-practice-observability` and `common-practice-trace-export` stacks.
- `alchemy.posthog.run.ts`: the `common-practice-analytics` stack for Common Practice production/Preview
  projects, dashboards and their charts.
- `test`: the opt-in Alchemy integration suite.
- `.github/workflows`: verification checks, pull-request Preview and manual production
  deployments.
- `docs`: the [documentation index](docs/README.md): design, runbooks, standards and dated evidence.
- `tools`: Effect command programs and lint enforcement tests.
- `.references`: ignored, locked upstream Effect and Alchemy source clones.
- `.agents/skills`: portable implementation guidance; `.claude/skills` links here.

Read [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [documentation](docs/README.md),
[lint policy](docs/standards/lint.md), [dependency choices](docs/standards/dependencies.md)
and the [deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md).

The pages introduce strategy, training, forward-deployed engineering,
deployments and agent builds. The cream layouts use a brown/gold halftone band
and navy cross pattern. The header and favicon use Paper's original Common
Practice tile and outlined wordmark. The decorative patterns repeat that same
tile. [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) records the confirmed audience and scope;
[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) records the implemented visual system.
[Appearance](packages/appearance/README.md) is a separate Effect-only package
with checked theme-switching actions. Other repositories can copy it and supply
their own runtime, identifiers and colours.
Preview Website responses and static assets carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.

Open sample training starts at `/training`: Claude for Beginners, Codex for
Beginners and Agentic AI for Legal Work. Each course has three chapters and six
pages, with explicit completion and browser-saved resume. Authored MDX lives in
`@content/training`; checked course logic and native progress atoms belong to
`@common-practice/training`. The [implementation ledger](docs/exec-plans/training-course-design.md)
records checks and release proof separately.

## AI work history

[Entire](https://entire.io) records both Codex and Claude Code chats and tool
activity alongside Git commits. This repository was configured with Entire CLI
0.11.3. Install Entire on each machine, then run from this checkout:

```sh
entire enable --agent codex --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire enable --agent claude-code --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire status
```

Open `/hooks` in Codex and approve the seven Entire commands. Both Codex and
Claude Code must start a fresh chat after setup so Entire can record each chat
from the beginning. `entire doctor` checks the installed commands and their
approval records.

The shared configuration is in `.entire/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json` and
`.claude/settings.json`. Run the setup commands above in every clone, so Git's
automatic recording commands are installed there too. Entire's local logs,
working chat copies and machine-specific settings are ignored by Git. Anonymous
usage reporting is off.

Commits create checkpoints, stored as separate Git references. The shared
settings select `origin` for chat uploads, so new working copies use the same
destination. Pushing to `origin` syncs those checkpoints, including chat text
and tool activity. Entire uploads to one selected remote; a push directly to
`upstream` does not upload the chat records. New chat activity after a push
waits for the next push.
Commit linking is automatic (`commit_linking: "always"`). For chats that change
files, finish the normal workflow with `git commit` and `git push origin`; the
installed Git commands create and upload the record. Ending a chat alone does
not publish it online. Chats without a file change can be published using the
explicit backfill workflow below.
This follows [Entire's documented workflow](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart).
Entire removes detected secrets before saving checkpoints, but this check can
miss things. Keep credentials out of chats and review what you share. Existing
chat history is not imported by the setup command above.

The repository's Entire page is <https://entire.io/gh/crcorbett/common-practice>. Its hosted
connection keeps a private copy of the repository in Australia (Sydney). This
connection is separate from the local recording setup. This checkout's `origin`
uses the Sydney mirror; the direct GitHub URL is preserved as `upstream`. The
mirror sends ordinary code pushes through to GitHub and stores chat records.
To configure another clone for the same mirror, run:

```sh
git remote rename origin upstream
entire repo remote add origin /gh/crcorbett/common-practice --cluster aws-ap-southeast-2.entire.io
entire enable --agent codex --checkpoint-push-remote origin --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire status
```

The destination command also repairs an older local choice. Check that
`entire status` names `origin`. Each existing working copy can have its own
`.entire/settings.local.json` override; keep its destination on `origin` too.

### Backfill existing chats

Entire CLI 0.10.5 can import existing Codex and Claude Code transcripts as
read-only checkpoints. Run a preview before importing:

```sh
entire import codex --dry-run
entire import claude-code --dry-run
entire import codex
entire import claude-code
```

The importer normally reads files changed in the past 30 days. It skips turns
already imported. Use `--session <id>` to select particular chats and `--path`
to select a transcript folder. Codex matches each chat's recorded working
folder; its default scan misses compressed archives and Common Practice's former Google
Drive location. The September 2026 backfill uses temporary, decompressed copies
of the selected chats, with only their initial working-folder field changed to
this checkout. Originals stay untouched. Claude Code's former project folder
can be selected directly with `--path`.

Imported chats can be searched and read, but cannot be resumed through Entire.
Sync them with the installed command `entire hooks git pre-push origin`, then
check the hosted Sessions page. This sync uploads checkpoint data without
pushing source changes. Use the Sydney mirror for `origin`: the initial backfill
reached GitHub, but its checkpoint references did not reach the hosted Sessions
page until they were pushed directly to the mirror. Ordinary Claude web, desktop
and Cowork chats have no direct importer in this CLI version.

## Live preview

Every hosted Preview stage has its own Alchemy-managed Website and API Workers.
After deploying stage `preview`, its Website address is
<https://common-practice-preview.coopercorbett.workers.dev>. See the deployment
runbook for Doppler configuration and the reviewed plan/deploy process.

Each same-repository pull request gets its own stage
`pr-<number>`, deployed by the **Pull request preview** workflow. The workflow
comments the Preview URL on the pull request and destroys the Preview when the
pull request closes. Fork pull requests are skipped.

`bun run test:integration` deploys the `integration` Preview, checks Home,
About, a missing page and the matching API’s `/pages`, then destroys it. It changes
Cloudflare, needs Doppler's `common-practice/stg_preview` credentials and is not part of
`verification`; run it only with authorisation.

## Production

Private source repository: <https://github.com/crcorbett/common-practice>.
Live website: <https://withcommonpractice.com>.
API: <https://api.withcommonpractice.com>; RPC `/rpc`, remote MCP `/mcp`.
Production uses stage `production` and Doppler config `common-practice/prd`:

```sh
bun run production:plan
bun run production:deploy --yes
```

GitHub Actions has a manual **Deploy production** workflow on `main`. It checks
the selected commit and uses the same native Alchemy scripts and cloud state.
See the deployment runbook for credential rotation and deployment coordination.

## Observability

Product analytics uses PostHog separately from request telemetry. The browser's
existing Effect Atom runtime records explicit page views and selected navigation
automatically on enabled deployments, while honouring Do Not Track. Browser
batches pass through `/ingest/e/` on the Website to reduce domain blocking;
occasional loss remains possible. The API counts its own requests and completed content reads,
with short sends in native Alchemy background work. Ordinary Previews and local
development keep collection off. A separate Alchemy stack owns production/Preview
PostHog projects and two private dashboards in each. See the
[analytics design](docs/exec-plans/posthog-analytics.md) and
[deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md) for setup and remaining proof.

Each Worker records its own response-ready requests. Cloudflare delivers logs and
traces to Axiom; counts come from request logs, with no custom metrics or Worker-side uploads. Website dashboards keep frontend counts separate from
backend activity in shared Axiom datasets, and five Common Practice dashboards read them: Request
Overview, Request Failures, Request Latency, Traffic and Telemetry Health.
Cached responses never reach the Worker, so the counts are Worker invocations,
not page views. Two production-only stacks own the pieces outside the Website,
and both need Common Practice's Axiom management credential in Doppler `common-practice/prd`:

```sh
bun run axiom:plan          # ingest token and dashboards
bun run axiom:deploy --yes
bun run trace:plan          # Cloudflare log and trace destinations
bun run trace:deploy --yes
```

Read the plan first, and apply only what it shows. The [observability
design](docs/exec-plans/observability.md) and [dashboard
design](docs/exec-plans/observability-dashboards.md) explain the choices. The
[deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md) has the checks to run after a
telemetry change, and dated proof is in
[docs/evidence/observability](docs/evidence/observability/2026-09-23-setup.md).

### Runtime settings

Alchemy supplies the existing named bindings to both applications. Keep the API
address tied to that stage's Backend output and each app's self address tied to
native `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`. Shared Config declarations and the checks they
reuse are described in [host settings](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#host-settings).

| Binding                          | Required behaviour                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`          | Use the declared stage. An invalid API stage stops startup. A missing or invalid Website stage returns its unavailable configuration result. The same declaration is reused by telemetry. |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`        | Supply the canonical API origin, without a trailing slash, credentials, path, query or fragment. Both apps and MCP reuse the checked declaration.                                         |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL`    | Supply the native Website self URL. Its root slash is accepted, but credentials, paths, queries and fragments are rejected.                                                               |
| `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG` | Missing, invalid or differently staged settings keep capture off. Production and test project checks are retained.                                                                        |

The API reads required settings during native startup. The Website reads public
settings once when its existing server runtime starts on the first request;
address or stage failures return its unavailable configuration result. Settings change
with a new runtime, so deploy the changed bindings together with the matching
code. Browser configuration contains only the checked public addresses and
capture settings; management credentials and telemetry tokens remain private.

credentials, PostHog projects or dashboards. Review the exact stage's plan and

Preview capture after stored-event checks.

Before release, run full verification and complete the three browser journeys,

not hosted proof. Roll back using the recorded pre-release revision through

### Commands

Run `bun run verification` first. Select the native Doppler profile locally,
or supply the config-scoped `DOPPLER_TOKEN` in CI. The stage-specific native plan
loads and checks the resolved configuration, including the account ID's form.
The old `production:check-env` and `pr:check-env` commands are removed: the
native provider preflight reads exported variables before stack secrets load
and cannot check this stage-specific configuration. Review the plan;
reject unexpected deletion, adoption, state-store upgrades or changes to another
application. After authorising that plan, use the corresponding deploy command:

```sh
bun run preview:plan
bun run preview:deploy --yes

bun run production:plan
bun run production:deploy --yes
```

The default deploy scripts omit `--yes`. It is needed for an authorised apply
in a non-interactive terminal. Native Alchemy recalculates the plan on apply.
Production serves from `withcommonpractice.com` (see Custom domain below).
Production scaffold content is indexable, so its placeholder wording may appear
in search results. Non-production Website responses and workers.dev static
assets carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.

`Cloudflare.state()` uses the account's native state store, partitioned by stack
and stage. Its first use can bootstrap resources, and a cold login can use a
temporary edge-preview session to read the state authentication secret.
Cloudflare requires Secrets Store Edit to attach that temporary secret binding;
Read only covers metadata and cannot complete a fresh login. Edit also permits
creating, changing and deleting secrets across the account. Cooper explicitly
approved this additional permission after a fresh GitHub run exposed the
Read-only limitation. See [Cloudflare access control](https://developers.cloudflare.com/secrets-store/access-control/).
A state-store upgrade or any other permission expansion remains a separate
maintenance task. Preserve the existing shared store and other applications;
do not switch to local state to bypass an authentication failure.

## Telemetry checks

Run these after a change to the telemetry Layer, the request observer, the
bindings or the dashboards. The design and reasons are in the
[observability plan](../exec-plans/observability.md). Record what you observe as a
dated file under `docs/evidence/observability/`, with the revision, stage, window
and figures. Do not copy provider state into a living document, and never put a
token in a command line, log or record.

**Authority.** The Preview deploy needs the reviewed plan and authorisation
(see Plan and deploy). The Axiom queries below only read. Use the read access of
the Common Practice management credential (`AXIOM_TOKEN` in `common-practice/prd`) or the Axiom web app.

### Log and trace delivery on a Preview

Request unique uncached Website URLs and one API machine route. Record the bounded
time window and deployment ids. Query Axiom for new JSON console request records
from both Workers; check stage, worker, response outcome and isolate identity.
Inspect the actual body envelope before using the shared dashboard reader. Verify
that logs contain no request bodies, credentials or raw user agents. Cloudflare
invocation records are separate and must not be counted as application records.

Wait for both signals to arrive before comparing counts. Confirm connected native
traces and no Worker-side calls to Axiom log or metric endpoints. There is no new
metric point to reconcile. Historical metric data is retained without live metric
panels. Log/trace delivery is best effort; successful requests alone do not prove
stored records, and records present do not establish lossless delivery.

### Isolate attributes on a Preview

Website request logs carry `requestSeq`, `isolateId` and `routeFamily`. The first
request in an isolate has sequence 1. Query those logs with the automatic root
span using their shared `trace_id`; wait for both signals before comparing counts.
The latency dashboard uses Cloudflare CPU time and log-derived cold/warm labels.
Missing logs remain unlabelled. The API retains native Alchemy Effect spans;
the Website has no custom span and no startup-time estimate. Do not treat root
span duration as visitor response time or infer cold starts from slow responses.

### Dashboards

The five Common Practice dashboards change only through `bun run axiom:plan` and
`bun run axiom:deploy --yes`. A plan for a dashboard-only change must show updates
to `CommonPracticeRequestOverview`, `CommonPracticeRequestFailures`,
`CommonPracticeRequestLatency`, `CommonPracticeTraffic` and `CommonPracticeTelemetryHealth`
and no other resource. Check the render, not only the plan:

1. Open each dashboard with `?v_stage=production`.
2. Keep the browser tab visible. A hidden tab never fills its panels, and a
   screenshot makes the tab visible.
3. Scroll every panel into view, because Axiom loads panels lazily.
4. Wait for the spinners to clear, then take the screenshot. One taken as a panel
   fills shows it blank.
5. Check a phone width (390 px) for the note, the tiles and the tables.

The [dashboard design](../exec-plans/observability-dashboards.md) says what each
panel answers and the rules its queries follow. To roll back, revert the change
and run `bun run axiom:deploy --yes` again. The dashboards are updated in place,
so a revert is an update, not a delete.

**Escalation.** A count that will not match, or a panel that stays empty, goes
into the plan's Open items with the query and window. Do not disable a check or
edit a dashboard in Axiom's web app to make it pass.

## Public page caching

Native `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` sets `cache.enabled: true`. The separate
`enable_request_signal` compatibility flag supports request cancellation; a
Preview test confirmed that page caching and MCP and RPC POSTs work with that
flag off. The cause of earlier POST hangs remains unproved. Cache entries stay
with one Worker version; a new deployment starts cold. Safe public HTML,
Markdown, social images and discovery text advertise the Site-style browser
and CDN lifetimes described in [architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).
Only the public page API list and its two checked detail paths join that

The private source repository is <https://github.com/crcorbett/common-practice>.
The manual **Deploy production** workflow runs on `main`, checks out the exact
event SHA, performs full verification, then plans and deploys with native Alchemy. Afterwards
it reads provider drift with `production:drift` and checks public pages. Pushing runs checks but
does not auto-deploy. The `production` GitHub environment allows only `main`.

GitHub holds only the read-only Doppler service token for `common-practice/prd` as its
`production` environment secret `DOPPLER_TOKEN`. The Cloudflare key stays in
Doppler. The Doppler token expires on 21 December 2026 at 09:25 UTC; rotate it
before then. Deployment credentials are available to plan, apply and state
readback, not dependency installation or checks.

Production and Preview workflows write only run metadata to the ignored `.env`:
`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITHUB_SHA`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`
and `BUILD_SHA`, plus `PULL_REQUEST` for Preview. This small shell step supplies

cleanup retain the environment's existing scoped `DOPPLER_TOKEN` and Preview's
`GITHUB_TOKEN` directly for provider sign-in. The workflows need no Doppler CLI.
Open PRs must include this cutover before their next deployment or cleanup.

The workflow serialises production runs with `cancel-in-progress: false`.
Local production deployments must run only while that workflow is idle;
GitHub concurrency does not lock this computer's terminal. The optional `force`
input defaults to false. Selecting it uses native `--force` for both the dry-run
plan and apply, allowing a deliberate rebuild of unchanged source. The final
state check is always non-forced.

### When GitHub Actions cannot start

Read the failed job's annotations first. If account usage, spending, payment or
runner limits prevented the job from starting, run the same checks and native
deployment commands locally. A failed build or test still needs fixing; local
execution does not turn a failed GitHub check into a passing one.

Use the exact reviewed commit from `main`, the pinned Bun version and frozen
lockfile. Confirm the production workflow is idle before a local apply. Use
the existing Doppler configuration and native Alchemy state; do not change
credentials, state ownership or branch protections to work around CI limits.

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run references:sync
bun run verification
bun run production:plan
```

Review the plan against the authorised change, then deploy and check the result:

```sh
bun run production:deploy --yes
bun run production:drift --no-input
COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_WEBSITE_URL=https://withcommonpractice.com \
COMMON_PRACTICE_VERIFY_API_URL=https://api.withcommonpractice.com bun run test:public
bun run production:plan
```

Record the blocked GitHub run, exact commit, local check results, reviewed plan,
apply, provider readback and public checks in dated evidence. Report GitHub's
blocked result separately from the local results. Use the same approach for an
authorised Preview, with its existing stage-specific commands and addresses.

Before replacing an Axiom ingestion token, check that the management key can
create API tokens and grant `ingest:create` on every requested dataset. A key
with only query/read access cannot create an ingestion token, even when it has
API-token creation access. A successful native plan does not prove that permission.
Any extra management access or use of another application's credential needs
specific owner authority. Keep the new ingestion token's permissions unchanged.

The active ingestion name is `common-practice-telemetry-ingest`; its retained
logical Alchemy address is `CommonPracticeTelemetryIngest`. The management key is
`common-practice-alchemy-management-20260923`, stored as `AXIOM_TOKEN` in

records the separately approved, one-off Site credential use. That approval
does not establish an ongoing Site credential source for these commands.

Treat native Alchemy state as secret material. A saved resource can contain
credentials, including values wrapped in `Redacted`. Do not print raw state or
pipe it into a command that might echo a failed input. Prefer independent
provider metadata and an explicit allowlist of non-secret fields for readback.

Rotate each Cloudflare token independently, replace its value in the matching
Doppler config, and prove the corresponding native command before revoking the
old Common Practice token. For production, also prove a fresh GitHub run. Keep token values
out of command arguments, logs and evidence; use standard input or a secure
secret-store integration. Do not revoke Site credentials as part of Common Practice rotation.

Rollback means restoring a reviewed known-good revision on `main` and running
the workflow, or deploying that revision locally through the same native
scripts and cloud state. Destroy requires explicit scope and authorisation.
The only destroy script is the guarded `pr:destroy`. Inspect state after
partial failure before retrying.

## Removal policies

Production's Website and Backend, Common Practice's Axiom ingest token, its five dashboards and the
`common-practice-axiom-traces` destination use `RemovalPolicy.retain`. Removing their
declaration or destroying their stack drops Alchemy's record but leaves the
cloud object running. Every Preview stays destroyable. A removal policy is not
a prop: a plan shows no change, and the next deploy of each stack records it.
Until then, the old destroy policy is still in state. The Axiom token has no
update API, so changing its props replaces it and leaves the old token live in
Axiom. Revoke that old token deliberately after the new one is proven.

Website and API URLs are checked through native `Output.mapEffect` when Alchemy
resolves them. Its callback has no error channel in the locked beta.81 release,
so an invalid URL stops resolution with `WebsiteOutputError` or `ApiOutputError`
as the fatal cause. A failed output check does not prove the Worker was rolled back.

The former `WebsiteOutput` Action declaration is removed. On the next separately
authorised native plan, Alchemy lists its saved Action record for deletion; the
following authorised apply drops that record without running the old Action
body or deleting a Worker. This follows beta.79's native `Plan.ts` and `Apply.ts`
Action-removal behaviour. Review that state-only removal alongside the Worker
changes. Do not manually edit cloud state or run a separate destroy to remove it.
Local URL tests prove checking, not removal of a hosted saved record.

Alchemy's CI guide suggests a `stacks/github.ts` stack that mints a scoped
Cloudflare token and writes it into GitHub secrets. Common Practice does not adopt it.
AGENTS.md keeps credentials in Doppler; that stack would move a long-lived
Cloudflare token into GitHub and into Alchemy state. It would also need an
admin credential with API-token write rights, which no Common Practice key has. GitHub keeps
only read-only Doppler service tokens, one per environment. Revisit this only if
Doppler stops being the credential source.

Alchemy and its Cloudflare SDK are unpatched. Stage-owned Website Workers use
the published native observability support rather than changing the Worker
Preview provider. After apply, read both Workers' settings independently and
query Axiom for their exact new versions. An existing Preview retaining old
settings is not proof that a new, unpatched Worker Preview would receive them.
